newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Exports by 30 S.Korean groups seen up 15 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Exports by 30 S.Korean groups seen up 15 pct in 97.

text.p: Exports by 30 major South Korean conglomerates are expected to rise 15 percent to $177 billion in 1997 against an estimated $153 billion this year, survey by the Federation of Korean Industries' (FKI) showed on Tuesday.

Improvements in technology and quality competitiveness, a rise in product demand from developing and industrialised nations, a stable foreign exchange rate and strengthening of price competitiveness are expected to boost exports next year, it said.
The survey also showed that conglomerates expect exports to grow a mere nine percent in 1996 compared with an earlier forecast of 21 percent for this year.

It attributed the slowdown to the sharp fall in prices of South Korea's major export items such as semiconductors, steel and petrochemicals, and the weakening of price competitiveness against Japanese exports because of the yen's depreciation against the dollar.

The survey added, however, that factors weighing on the overall export outlook included high production costs such as high wages, interest rates and distribution costs combined with a decline in export prices.
